name: DealCloud

field_reviews.reason: Live api.docs.dealcloud.com/docs/token: 'DealCloud uses the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow to generate a bearer token'; POST with grant_type=client_credentials, client_id and the user's apiKey as client_secret.

Token docs confirm client-credentials flow using client_id + apiKey, returning a bearer token (15-minute expiry) used in the Authorization header; API key self-served from user Profile after an admin enables the API capability. MCP additionally uses per-user OAuth sign-in.

No self-serve signup, no free trial, no public pricing anywhere on intapp.com — only 'Schedule a demo'. Third-party contract data (Vendr/GetApp/prospeo) confirms sales-only procurement with contracts roughly $85K-$1.4M/year. This is a genuine hard commercial gate, not a login-gated-docs artifact: the API docs themselves are public but credentials exist only inside a purchased site.
Public docs cover Data and Schema APIs (api/rest/v4), User Management, Publications, Relationship Intelligence Import, and Site Backup APIs with distinct OAuth scopes.

REST APIs confirmed at api/rest/v1 and v4; official MCP server confirmed. Note: the MCP server internally exposes GraphQL tooling (search_schema, introspect, execute_query), but no standalone customer-facing GraphQL endpoint is documented, so omitting graphql from api_protocols is reasonable.

Verified on the vendor's own docs domain (api.docs.dealcloud.com/mcp and /mcp/getting-started): 'DealCloud MCP Server — client preview starting July 2026', requires DealCloud with Celeste license plus Manage MCP Servers / MCP Access permissions, per-user OAuth, and all tools currently read-only. This is vendor-owned, not community. Caveat: it is a client preview, not GA.

For a firm that already licenses DealCloud, the REST API is fully documented and credentials are admin-enabled self-serve; the sales gate is captured in primary_blocker rather than the verdict, consistent with the draft's stated convention.
Enterprise sales-led procurement is the only path to credentials; no trial or self-serve tier exists. MCP further requires the Celeste license.

notes: High-risk claims both held up. (1) Official vendor MCP: confirmed live on api.docs.dealcloud.com — vendor-owned docs, July 2026 client preview, Celeste license + MCP Access gating, per-user OAuth, read-only tools. (2) Hard commercial gate: confirmed no trial/self-serve/public pricing via intapp.com demo-only flow and independent pricing benchmarks ($85K-$1.4M annual contracts). Also re-verified the token endpoint doc (client credentials, apiKey as secret, 15-min tokens, scoped APIs).
